title: Kenyan Eid Mahamri
community: Coastal Muslim Kenyan communities at Eid
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: Eid Mahamri is the celebration version of KEN015 (Kenyan Mahamri). The technique is identical — for Eid, the coconut milk is richer, the cardamom more generous, and a touch of rose water may be added. They are made in larger quantities, shared with neighbours and the needy as part of the Eid tradition.

desc: Kenyan Eid Mahamri — the beloved Swahili coconut doughnuts made with extra richness for Eid celebrations. Fragrant with cardamom and rose water, fried golden and hollow, shared generously with family, neighbours, and the needy. The Eid morning of the coast begins with mahamri.
longDesc: On Eid morning along the Kenyan coast, the smell of mahamri frying in coconut oil fills the air before dawn. These golden, hollow, cardamom-fragrant doughnuts are made in enormous quantities — shared with family, given to neighbours, and distributed to those in need as an act of charity that is central to the Eid spirit. For Eid, the mahamri are richer, more fragrant, and made with extra love.
ingredients: 1 tsp dry yeast or 2 tsp baking powder
½ tsp rose water — the Eid touch, optional
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm coconut milk. Rest 10 minutes until foamy.
Combine flour, cardamom, and salt. Make a well in the centre.
Pour in the yeast mixture and rose water if using.
Mix to a soft dough. Knead for 8—10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and rest in a warm place for 1.5—2 hours until doubled.
Punch down. Divide into golf ball-sized pieces. Roll into rounds.
Fry in batches for 3—4 minutes, turning, until deeply golden on all sides.
The hollow interior is formed by the steam expansion during frying.
chefTips: Warm coconut milk activates the yeast more effectively.
The hollow interior is the signature of perfect mahamri — achieved by correct dough hydration and oil temperature.
For Eid, double the recipe — there will never be enough.
commonMistakes: Too cold coconut milk — yeast does not activate.
Too hot oil — outside burns before hollow interior forms.
cookingScience: See KEN015 for the full cooking science of mahamri. For the Eid version, the rose water contains geraniol and citronellol — volatile aromatic compounds that evaporate quickly but leave a floral fragrance that signals celebration.
sustainabilityTips: Making mahamri to share is a zero-waste act — excess are always given away.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Can be stored for 1 day.
reheating: Warm in oven at 150°C for 8 minutes.
culturalNote: Eid mahamri is the fragrance of celebration on the Kenyan coast — the smell of cardamom and coconut frying before dawn on Eid morning is one of the most culturally significant aromas in Swahili coastal life. The act of sharing mahamri with neighbours and the needy is as important as the eating.
